messages.author: de1d27fecc0bbd03
messages.subject: Comparing disparity values
parts:
Hello,
I would like to compare diparities of different vertebral regions (cervical, thoracic...) with a different number of landmarks for a set of species. We have computed two different sets of Procrustes ANOVA (procD.lm):
(i) using vertebral identity (e.g., cervical3*cervical4*....) as a factor for each region (cervical,thoracic...).
(ii) using species (species1*species2*species3) as a factor for each region.
Our goal is to compare if morphological variability for each region is explained by interspecific or intra-regional varibility -i.e., if differences between vertebrae for each region (e.g., cervical3-cervical7 or thoracic1-thoracic11) are larger than the differences between species (e.g., cervical_species1-cervical_species11 or thoracic_species1-thoracic_species11 and so on).
To do this, we have computed the Zscore obtained from procD.lm from each Procustes ANOVA, but we are not sure if this is the best option of variability comparison. Moreovoer, we do not know how to compare it statistically, we guess that a bootstrap procedure is needed here but I wonder if you could give any insight on how to reshufle the data.
Best wishes and thank you very much in advance,
borja
PS: Please, note that we cannot digitize the same number of landmarks in all the vertebrae as we lose a lot of morphological information in some regions.

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Comparing disparity values
parts:
Dear Borja,

Are you performing GPA on all vertebrae coordinates together?  If so, I’m not sure comparing disparities (Procrustes variances) among different vertebrae would make much sense as the GPA - not evolution - could be most responsible for variation in disparities among vertebrae with different densities of landmarks.

More generally, having different numbers of landmarks for different vertebrae, both within an individual and across species, makes it hard to think of a logical comparative analysis.  Maybe somebody else will have a good idea, but just be careful with interpreting disparity in parts of configurations that were influenced by GPA performed on entire configurations.

Best,
Mike
